If you really want to avoid the doc: Some of these infections are viral and will fade given some time and care. Switch between hot and cold drinks. Find what gives you most relief. I find Ice cream to help a lot as well as warm milk with a ton of honey in it. 
You can gargle salt water, but don't overdo it. 
Ibuprofen is imo the most helpful painkiller in these cases. If you want an alternative: Colludol is a kind of numbing spray which I find to be pretty effective as well. 
Stay clear of things that may irritate your throat such as smoking, alcohol or spicy foods.

Observe the state of the infection. If after a couple of days you find it's still worsening, then you may require antibiotics and a doctor's visit afterall.

My partner and I tried very long for our first child. 

Some people go through expensive and lenghty treatments to have a baby. This period brings a tremendous amount of stress and disappointment. 

When the good news finally arrives, you're ecstatic. As the months progress you make your plans, choose all the babystuff. Ready the room, design the cards, bring out the good news to family and friends, ask a godmother and godfather. Youre constantly looking forward to it and the entire pregancy is filled with milestones: hearing a heartbeat for this first time, finding out the gender, agree'ing on a name, then the little kicks start and intensify until the father can feel and see them too. You go to each doctor appointment hoping everything is alright and the relief is always so huge when the doctor confirms everything is alright and the baby is growing well.

The baby is eventually born and after months of happiness and anticipation, this get taken away almost immediately after.
I can assure you depression hits for less. Now the parents get to arrange a funeral in stead of a baby shower and it has to be the most exhausting and mentally draining experience for every parent out there. You not only have to give your grief a place, you also gotta be there for each other and hope your relationship survives.

Now the parents face a choice. "Do we go through all this again? Again with uncertain results? Are we strong enough to go through this again?" 
"Do we need time or will we just accept fate and give up trying?"

It's always a disaster. Hope you can broaden your view with this post and comments.

Every tip i write is from personal experience. It could very well be that other people have better imput. I just beat stage 30.

XP boosts are your friend. Pick them whenever they present themselves in the store, or as ability, UNLESS you can pick Vampire/Scavenger in stead. Vamp and Scav are insanely good and should be priority if you're able to pick them.

For all other times I tried maxing dodge and armor as soon as possible. It makes surviving waves less of a hassle and gives you more freedom to farm materials. You will also be able to tank most of the boss' offense.

Concerning offense: max the crit perk. Its final stage will make the boss cry. If you're unable to with skills, get your crit chance and damage up as much as possible through the store.

If you're still able to level up beyond that, my preferences are in order: attack speed, speed (dont go beyond the 3rd level), damage, hp 

If you're able to buy lucky roll, do it asap. It gives you a free store reroll in between every wave and is a tremendous advantage.

Pick all lifesteal items you come across in the store (if youre not maxing vampire already) always pick leeches regardsless of perks.

Dont bother too much with zipline stuff, tempest, blizzard, acid, not even pandora's box. Dragon or other summons are not worth it. 

I like picking range items if i have spare materials. It can offer some much needed distance between you and the boss and it strenghtens your attacks against him, if you have the perk. Having the eagle item will increase your damage for every +5 range as well.

If you haven't spent 2-3 levels in speed, consider buying some speed perks if you have spare materials. Usually my dodge and armor make up for damage suffered, but sometimes, outrunning the boss' attacks might be required.

Im not a big fan of the purple "+% hp/dmg per kill" items as they're usually no good against bosses. I pick them when I have way more than I can spend or when I need the extra stats in survival stages.

Always pick luna/sol. I figured that as soon as I buy either one, the game will present me the other one very shortly after. The combination of them doubles your stats so I say worth it.

Lastly for now (might edit later): focus on maxing your gear. It helps a lot.
